title: The Kővári–Sós–Turán theorem
statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph whose vertex set has $n$ elements, and write $e(G)$ for its number of edges. Let $m \ge 1$ be an integer. If
\[
e(G) > \tfrac{1}{2}\,(m-1)^{1/m}\, n^{\,2 - 1/m} + \tfrac{1}{2}\,(m-1)\, n,
\]
then $G$ contains the complete bipartite graph $K_{m,m}$ as a subgraph.
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph on n vertices
m is a positive integer (1 ≤ m)
the edge count e(G) strictly exceeds ½(m−1)^{1/m} n^{2−1/m} + ½(m−1)n
replaced:

$\nu$\textasciicircum{}\{2-1/m\})/2 + ((m-1)$\nu$)/2}, then \texttt{G} contains
\texttt{K\_\{m,m\}}.}
